reviewers.persona: Prüferin (lizenzierte Goethe-A1-Prüferin, Start Deutsch 1): Prüfungstreue, Rubrik, Aufgabenklarheit
Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: We read every German string: the Folge, 3 × 10 dialogue lines, the form text, 6 exam texts, the check lines, all prompts, options, explanations, instructions, situations, endLines, redemittel, the three rule cards the unit shows, and the unit's 35 lexicon cards. We solved all 98 authored items blind: start gist 1; per LS 5 input + 4 structured + 11 pool + 5 reserve; 6 H1 items; 8 Check + 3 proof items. We also solved the 5 S1 form fields. Each was solved from promptDe plus options/tiles/audio line only. The doubtful answers were run through the real grader src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js („Herr Richter ist kein Lehrer.“ → wrong; postcode, phone and number-word variants → correct). The H1 block, the Sp1 task and the S1 form were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1: 6 items, 3 options, 2 plays, textWords 32–53, pictorial → scaffolded text variant in a1.1; sp1: monologue, prep 0, rubric sd1-sp1, intro + spelling + number; s1: 5 fields, situation 36–48 words). We recounted the words of the exam texts (39/46/39/40/40/49 and S1 ≈ 42). The tasks are original, and no official Modellsatz wording was found. We checked the grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json (g.negation-nicht and g.ja-nein-frage new at u02; g.possessiv-mein-dein u03; g.kein u06; g.trennbare-verben u07; g.possessiv-sein-ihr with Genitiv-s bei Namen a1.2-u03), new-word load against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 ±10 %; 35 here), and roles against a1.1/lexicon.json. Can-dos were checked against registries/cando/a1.json, cast facts against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json, and the story against u01 (cliffhanger → u02), u03, u05 (Berliner Straße 21 = Arjun's WG), u08 and u12. The unit was checked against curriculum/a1-1.json u02. Exemplar: u04 and its trail r1–r5, plus the u01 r1 review. Every earlier finding class was checked for recurrence and named where it recurs. Arithmetic and read-backs recomputed: 20→21, 16→60, 70→17, 34→43, 12 in the A1 course and 100 in the school; phone formats 0341 (Leipzig), 0090 5xx (TR mobile), 04105 (Leipzig).

validator.result: OK (no blocker findings) — 40 rules: 32 pass, 0 fail, 3 warn (ALL-02: 1 advisory, cd.a1.nachfragen proven by an item alone → F19; GRM-04: 48 advisory → F07, F08, F20; LEX-02: 17 ratchet → F21), 5 skipped (ITM-08 no caseSensitive item; CON-06 facts[] empty; COV-1/4/5 level-scope). Not implemented as rule files, so checked by hand here: CON-01/02/04/05, LNG-01…04, TXT-01, AUD-01…05, TIM-01…05, and the ITM-01 error-correction rail of u04 r5-F01.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 0 BLOCKER, 5 MAJOR, 16 MINOR. Every key is right. The H1 block matches sd1.json in items, options, plays, word band and a/b/c balance (b a c b c a). The Sp1 task now asks for all three scored parts (the u01 r1-F01 class is closed here). The S1 form has exactly five fields from a 42-word situation. Every read-back is consistent, and du/Sie follows the cast bible. The scenes have life: the phone chaos with Emre, „zwo“, Priya as participant number 100, and a cliffhanger that u03 picks up. Five things stop exit. (1) Correction items still use a bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ (the u04 r5-F01 rail was never written), and ls1-p10 rejects the correct „Herr Richter ist kein Lehrer.“ (F01). (2) ls2-s02 is ambiguous against the Lernschritt's own model sentence (F02). (3) The form can-do says „mit meinen Angaben“, but the proving Aufgabe forbids the learner's own data, and no own-data form exists in the unit (F03). (4) A u02 word card says Priya works at the reception desk, which contradicts LS3 and is the distractor of ls3-i05 (F04, lexicon owner). (5) The u01 „Was sprichst du?“ calque recurs on an exam stem (F05). Most minors are exemplar classes recurring: task-surface words above level, genitive and „kurze“ on instruction and exam surfaces, receptive lemmas typed, unheard H1 distractors, and unlogged plan deviations.

counts.note: unitOwned = the fix edits u02.json. F04 is the lexicon owner's (lx.empfang.example). F09's number-block roles, F20 and F21 belong to the lexicon owner, the rule-smith and the level reviewer. F16's phone-number part belongs to u08/u12, with the cast bible's record of the data. The rule-card parts of F07/F10 belong to the rule-cards owner.

findings.quote: ls1-p10 „Korrigieren Sie: „Herr Richter nicht ist Lehrer.““ → accepted only „Herr Richter ist nicht Lehrer.“ · ls1-p09 (same LS) accepts „Lehrerin ist Priya nicht.“
findings.problem: This is the a1.1-u04 r5-F01 class again. The German prompt says only „Korrigieren Sie:“, so it does not tell the learner what to fix. „Herr Richter ist kein Lehrer.“ is a correct correction, and it is the more usual German for a profession without an article (Duden: kein is the norm, nicht is used with contrast). The real grader marks it WRONG (tagged v2-inv, so the learner is sent to the word-order repair card). „Lehrer ist Herr Richter nicht.“ is also a grammatical V2 correction. The builder item ls1-p09 in the same Lernschritt accepts exactly this order („Lehrerin ist Priya nicht.“), but the correction item rejects it. The exemplar now names the category on every correction („Korrigieren Sie den Artikel: …“). This unit uses bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ on four items and „Korrigieren Sie die Frage/den Satz“ on three more. The u04 r5-F01 rail was never written: ITM-01 still has no check on error_correction prompts. So the validator passes this unit, and the gate hole remains.
findings.fix: ls1-p10: „Korrigieren Sie die Wortstellung: „Herr Richter nicht ist Lehrer.““, and accept „Lehrer ist Herr Richter nicht.“ with acceptedWhy (the same rule as ls1-p09). Or keep the prompt and accept „Herr Richter ist kein Lehrer.“ with acceptedWhy. Name the category on the other six items too: ls1-r04 „… die Wortstellung“, ls2-p10/ls2-r05 „… die Wortstellung in der Frage“, ls3-p10/ls3-r05 „… die Verbform“, c07 „… das Wort“ („Ich bin Lehrer.“ → Lehrerin). Give ls3-p10 and ls3-r05 an errorTag as well (see u01 r1-F15 on the missing Personalendung tag).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01 (the a1.1-u04 r5-F01 rail, still unwritten): an error_correction item whose errorTag/errorTags[0] is v2-inv, verb-final, connector-position, satzklammer, gender-article or case, or that has no errorTag, must name the corrected category in promptDe („die Wortstellung“, „die Verbform“, „den Artikel“, „die Endung“, „das Wort“), unless every alternative correction is in accepted[] with acceptedWhy. Also: every order that a sentence_building item of the same unit accepts for the same pattern must be accepted by the correction item. Failing fixture: a1.1-u02 ls1-p10. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.quote: „Emre sagt: „In İzmir.“ Was fragt Herr Richter?“ — options „Wo wohnen Sie?“ (key) / „Wohnen Sie in Leipzig?“ / „Ist das richtig?“ · modelSentence of the same LS: „Wohnen Sie in Leipzig? – Nein, in İzmir.“
findings.problem: The item is ambiguous. The distractor „Wohnen Sie in Leipzig?“ is the question of the Lernschritt's own model sentence, and that model pairs it with the answer „(Nein,) in İzmir“. In the scene, Herr Richter never asks „Wo wohnen Sie?“. He asks „Wohnen Sie nicht in Leipzig?“, and Emre answers „… Ich wohne in İzmir“. A learner who answers from the scene or from the model sentence picks b. „Wohnen Sie in Leipzig?“ – „In İzmir.“ is also a normal elliptical reply in speech. The explanation claims that an item of information answers only a W-question, and the unit's own model contradicts this.
findings.fix: Detach the stem from the scene, and give b a yes/no question that cannot take a place as its answer. Stem: „Die Antwort ist: „In İzmir.“ Welche Frage passt?“ Options: „Wo wohnen Sie?“ / „Lernen Sie online?“ / „Ist das richtig?“.

findings.problem: The only proof of the unit's productive written can-do is an Aufgabe that forbids what the can-do states. The S1 task correctly follows the exam format (transferring another person's data from a text). But nowhere in the unit does the learner write their own name, address, phone number or job into a form. LS3 only shows Priya's form to read. The own data appears only in speech (ls1-mo, Sp1). No other a1.1 unit carries cd.a1.formular-person, so the level never proves the can-do. This is the u04 r1-F07 / u01 r1-F02 class: the can-do is claimed but not performed.
findings.fix: Add a short second part to LS6 (or turn the LS2 written micro-output into it): „Jetzt Ihr Formular: Familienname, Vorname, Wohnort, Telefonnummer, Beruf.“ The KI checks form and spelling only, and the learner may use invented data (see F18). Point proofs[2] to that part. Keep the Emre form as the S1 exam practice.
findings.proposedRule: ALL-02: when a can-do's text names the learner's own data („meine/meinen Angaben“, „über mich“), its proving Aufgabe must not be a task whose data come from a third-person stimulus only (sd1.s1 situationDe about another person). Failing fixture: a1.1-u02 check.proofs[2].

findings.quote: „Priya ist nicht Lehrerin.“ · „Herr Richter ist nicht Lehrer.“ · „Ich bin nicht Schüler. Ich bin Student.“ · „Er spricht nicht Deutsch.“ · rc.negation-nicht „nicht steht vor dem Wort, das nicht stimmt“
findings.problem: The unit makes nicht + an article-less noun the default negation of nouns. „X ist nicht Lehrerin“ is grammatical, but without a contrast German uses kein. The rule card states the position rule without limits („vor dem Wort, das nicht stimmt“), so a learner derives ✗„Ich habe nicht Formular / nicht Nummer“. In u06, rc.kein then teaches that nouns without an article take kein. This is a §9.5 case: a simplification that becomes false. The spine and the plan chose „Ich bin nicht Lehrerin.“, so the unit's author followed them. The unit can still keep every such line contrastive, as the rule card's own model does („Ich bin nicht Lehrerin. Ich bin Ärztin.“).
findings.fix: ls1-p09: tiles for „Priya ist nicht Lehrerin. Sie ist Rezeptionistin.“ (two sentences, or a builder with the contrast as a fixed tile), or a non-noun target („Priya ist nicht hier.“). ls1-p10: see F01. Folge gist distractor: „Er ist nicht in Leipzig.“ instead of „Er spricht nicht Deutsch.“. readAloud: keep the contrast pair. Rule-cards owner: add one line to rc.negation-nicht: „Nomen mit ein oder ohne Artikel: kein (Einheit 6).“

findings.quote: h1-01 „0341 62 58 17“ (62 is never said) · h1-03 „33“ (never said) · strategy card „Achten Sie auf „nein“ und „nicht“: Die Antwort kommt oft danach.“
findings.problem: This is the u04 r1-F19 / u01 r1-F12 class. Two of six H1 distractors are never heard, so a learner who only recognises numbers they heard can eliminate them. In 4 of the 6 texts the key follows „nein/nicht“, and the strategy card turns that pattern into a rule. The exemplar's card now teaches the opposite habit („Oft hören Sie alle drei Antworten – aber nur eine passt zur Frage.“), which is what the real Teil demands.
findings.fix: h1-01: make the third option a variant the learner hears, e.g. „0341 26 85 17“, with the clerk first misreading „achtundfünfzig“ as „fünfundachtzig“. h1-03: let the clerk first read back „dreiunddreißig“ („33? – Nein, …“), or use the options „43 / 34 / 3“ with „drei“ heard. findings.quote: „Am Telefon ist „zwo“ oft „zwei“.“ · „Ich verstehe nicht.“ · „Lehrerin für Englisch“ · „Buchstabieren Sie, bitte.“ · form „Postleitzahl, Wohnort: 04105 Leipzig / Land: Indien“
findings.problem: Isolated unidiomatic phrasing on model surfaces. The zwo explanation says it backwards ('on the phone, zwo is often zwei'). On a bad line a German says „Ich verstehe Sie nicht.“. „Englischlehrerin“ is the usual word. „Buchstabieren Sie bitte.“ takes no comma. On a German registration form, „Land“ directly under the address reads as the country of the address, so „Land: Indien“ under a Leipzig address looks like an error. The field for a country of origin is „Herkunftsland“ or „Staatsangehörigkeit“.
findings.fix: „Am Telefon sagt man oft „zwo“ für „zwei“.“ · Folge l03/l10 „Ich verstehe Sie nicht.“ · t4 „Und du bist Englischlehrerin?“ · „Buchstabieren Sie bitte.“ · form: „Herkunftsland: Indien“ (gloss), placed above the address block.

findings.quote: det.bestimmter-artikel on „das Formular“, „die Adresse“ … (≈ 38×) and on „ist das Emre?“ · det.possessiv-sein-ihr on „Kurs habt ihr heute.“ · det.trennbare-verben on „Wir lernen zusammen“ · det.imperativ-sie on „Lesen Sie“, „Buchstabieren Sie“
findings.problem: Most advisories are false positives. (a) The definite-article detector fires on every article + noun before its u04 intro, which cannot be avoided in u01–u03 and buries real hits. (b) „das“ as a demonstrative pronoun is read as an article. (c) The pronoun „ihr“ + Kurs is read as a possessive. (d) The adverb „zusammen“ is read as a separable prefix (the u04 r1-F24 „macht zusammen“ class, still open). (e) Imperatives licensed as a chunk since u01 are still reported (u04 r4-F08). The real hits are „kurze“, the split ausfüllen and „Meine/Ihre Telefonnummer“, all covered in F07/F08.
findings.fix: No unit change beyond F07/F08. Rule-smith: det.bestimmter-artikel reports only an article the learner chooses (typed gap or error correction), not article + noun in input or tiles. Add fixtures for the other four patterns.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-04 fixtures at a1.1-u02: „Oh, ist das Emre?“, „Kurs habt ihr heute.“, „Wir lernen zusammen, ja?“, „Buchstabieren Sie bitte.“ and „Hier ist das Formular.“ produce no advisory. The test runs over all registered courses.
